title: Oatcakes with goat's cheese and roast rhubarb

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Oats, wholemeal flour, butter, goat's cheese, honey, orange and rhubarb are all plain home staples with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Forced rhubarb, soft goat's cheese and everything else are everyday stock at Tesco in January.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a bowl, baking trays and a knife, and rubbing in and pressing out a dough is well within a beginner's reach.

works.reason: The 200g oats, 50g flour, 60g butter and 100ml water make a workable oatcake dough for 12 pieces, 25 minutes at 190°C will crisp it, and 12 minutes is right for 300g roast rhubarb, so this is a sensible snack for four.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes covers rubbing in, pressing out, zesting, chopping rhubarb and spreading, and the 25-minute bake matches the steps.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the salt and thyme, appears in the steps, and nothing unlisted is used apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: Forced rhubarb is at its peak in late January, and at 300g roasted it is clearly the point of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Wholegrain oatcakes with cheese and fruit make a satisfying, real-food afternoon snack that isn't mostly sugar.
